domain.location: Complete draft-v5.md (278 lines), mechanism sections, evidence matrix, evaluator/generalization discussion, economics appendix and conditional adoption guidance
domain.basis: Reviewed the entire report and its current DGM revision for the technical domain of automated improvement, evaluator design and generalization. DGM is correctly separated into frozen foundation weights, editable agent code and fixed outer search; the original paper sections 3/4, appendix C.3/E.1 and released DGM_outer.py/self_improve_step.py support archive filtering, external o1 diagnosis, adaptive benchmark use, disclosed budgets and the distinction between paper agents and code generation defaults. The current opening, DGM discussion and evidence matrix now expressly include repeated downstream attempts, another foundation model's selection, and conditioning later attempts on earlier ones; 20→50 and 14.2→30.7 are therefore treated as results of the combined evolved system, without an unsupported matched-inference attribution. AlphaEvolve's original sections 2.3–2.5/3.3 support database score/output history, exploitation/diversity, Flash/Pro roles, evaluator cascades, feasibility outside the editable Borg ranking, a half-shape optimization/evaluation split, and distinct 23% kernel/1% overall training effects. Its RTL example explicitly retains the downstream-synthesis counterfactual. Dated product/impact records support the bounded deployment discussion. Promptbreeder's official paper pp.4,8,16–17,27 and original Table 1/Figure 4 images support binary tournament selection, training/test boundaries, PaLM 2-L baseline identities, 83.9/66.5/65.5, the limited population-mean-fitness ablation and 301m/6m token account; these are not promoted into universal operator effects. SCoRe's previously checked original two-attempt training protocol and wrong→right/right→wrong distinctions are accurately carried into this report. HarnessPro v2 sections 4.3/5.1–5.5 distinguish synthesized fixed tests from official held-out grading, 10 training tasks, 59/100/100 held-out tasks, ProgramBench fractional-test aggregation, failure recall, terminal execution cost, and selected artifacts from the full optimizer. Released README and terminal hook substantiate the runtime scope. Rethinking v1 sections 4.1–4.4/A.4–A.5 use common initial harness and K=5 rollouts, distinguish selection from oracle pass@5, and retain the 45/10/34 split and small observed 0.6-point average transfer rather than a universal impossibility conclusion. The existing arithmetic source/results were read without execution; the 4.5-point/33.9% comparison, SCoRe differences, transfer average and Amdahl examples use the stated denominators. The adoption guidance follows these domain limits; no remaining necessary domain correction was found.
